comments.content: `PSModuleInfo` does not override `Equals`/`GetHashCode`, so this `HashSet<PSModuleInfo>` uses reference identity. The filter therefore only works while `Get-Module` returns the exact same object instances that are cached in `curModule.NestedModules`. That holds today because `AddModuleToModuleTables` stores one instance in both places, but it is a fragile assumption: any path that yields a different instance for the same module (e.g. a nested module re-imported/reloaded, or results merged from `TopLevelSessionState.ModuleTable` in `ModuleIntrinsics.GetModuleCore`) makes the filter silently stop filtering and the original issue reappears. The engine already defines `PSModuleInfoComparer` (Name + Guid + Version) for exactly this comparison and `RemoveModuleCommand` uses it; consider using it here (or compare `Path`) so the check does not depend on object identity.

comments.content: This filter is keyed on `EngineSessionState.Module`, so it drops the nested modules of *whatever* module happens to own the session state where completion runs, not just PSReadLine's internals. If a user invokes completion from inside their own script module (e.g. calling `TabExpansion2` from a module function, or a custom host/prompt module with nested modules), `Get-Module -Name <tab>` and `Remove-Module <tab>` only query loaded modules (`loadedModulesOnly: true`, unlike `Import-Module`/`Get-Command -Module` which get a second `-ListAvailable` pass), so that module's own nested modules — which are genuinely loaded and removable — disappear from the completion results. Consider narrowing the filter to the intended case (e.g. only skip nested modules of an engine/PSReadLine module, or only modules that are not independently visible from the top-level session state) so user module nesting is unaffected.
